question: I sold my home in 2025. Do I still report the sale to CRA if it was my principal residence the whole time?
generated_answer:
As of 2016, the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requires you to report the sale of your principal residence on your tax return, even if the property was your principal residence for the entire time you owned it. This is due to changes made to the Income Tax Act.

When you sell your principal residence, you need to report the disposition on Schedule 1 of your tax return (T1) and complete Form T2091, "Designation of a Property as a Principal Residence by an Individual (Other Than a Personal Trust)". You'll also need to provide basic information about the sale, such as:

* The address of the property
* The year you acquired the property
* The year you sold the property
* The proceeds of disposition (the sale price)

You'll claim the principal residence exemption on the form, which will typically eliminate any capital gains tax owing on the sale.

Even though you won't have to pay capital gains tax if the property was your principal residence the entire time, reporting the sale is still required. This helps the CRA verify that the property was indeed your principal residence and ensures you're eligible for the exemption.

Keep in mind that if you have a complex situation, such as a change in use of the property (e.g., renting it out for a period) or if you're claiming the exemption for multiple properties, you may need to provide additional information or seek professional advice.

For your specific situation, since you sold your home in 2025, you'll need to report the sale on your 2025 tax return, which is typically due by April 30, 2026. Be sure to keep all relevant documents, such as the sale agreement and any other supporting records, in case the CRA requests them.
